# Azure Confidential Compute

Terraform pattern module for Azure Confidential Virtual Machines.

The root module composes the [confidential virtual machine submodule](modules/confidential-virtual-machine/README.md).
It accepts a map of Linux or Windows VM definitions, applies default locations and tags, and creates:

- One network interface and confidential VM per definition.
- Optional managed data disks and their attachments.
- Optional Azure Backup protection using an existing Recovery Services vault and VM backup policy.

The root module does not create resource groups, virtual networks, subnets, backup vaults, or backup policies.
The [examples](examples/README.md) create their own prerequisites.

## Prerequisites

- Terraform and provider versions satisfying the generated requirements below.
- An authenticated Azure identity with permissions to manage the requested resources.
- An existing resource group and subnet for each VM. The subnet must be usable by the VM's network interface.
- A confidential-compute-compatible VM size and image available in the selected region and zone, with sufficient subscription quota.
- An SSH public key or password for Linux; a password is required for Windows. Protect Terraform state because passwords are retained in state.
- For backup, an existing compatible Recovery Services vault and VM backup policy, and permissions to configure VM protection.
  Use an Enhanced (`V2`) policy for the VM configuration in the backup-enabled example. The module associates the
  supplied policy ID; it does not create policies or upgrade Standard (`V1`) policies to Enhanced.
  For daily/weekly Enhanced policies, explicitly configure instant-restore retention shorter than vaulted retention.

The current VM, networking, data-disk, and backup implementation uses the AzureRM provider.
AzAPI is used for subscription-scoped telemetry deployments. Configure the providers in the calling Terraform root;
this reusable module does not configure them. The legacy `/azurerm` module address is distinct from these provider requirements.

## Usage

The following module call assumes this repository is checked out in a directory named
`terraform-azurerm-avm-ptn-confidential-compute` beneath the calling Terraform root.
Replace the resource names, subnet ID, and public-key path with your own values.

```hcl
module "confidential_compute" {
  source = "./terraform-azurerm-avm-ptn-confidential-compute"

  location = "eastus"
  tags = {
    environment = "development"
  }
  confidential_virtual_machines = {
    cvm1 = {
      name                = "cvm-eastus-001"
      resource_group_name = "rg-confidential-eastus-001"
      subnet_resource_id  = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-confidential-eastus-001/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/vnet-confidential-eastus-001/subnets/workload"
      source_image_reference = {
        publisher = "Canonical"
        offer     = "0001-com-ubuntu-confidential-vm-jammy"
        sku       = "22_04-lts-cvm"
        version   = "latest"
      }
      admin_username       = "azureuser"
      admin_ssh_public_key = file("~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub")
      size                 = "Standard_DC2as_v5"
    }
  }
}
```

For runnable Terraform roots, see the [default Windows Server 2025 example](examples/default/README.md), which creates
its resource group, network, and a 128-GB data disk, and the [backup-enabled Windows Server 2025 example](examples/backup-enabled/README.md).
Both examples default to East US (`eastus`) without random region selection. Their VM sizes differ; verify quota and
image availability for the selected example. The root module itself does not impose an East US default.

## Configuration behavior

- Every VM needs either its own `location` or the root `location`.
- VM-level `tags` replace, rather than merge with, root `tags`. Data-disk tags similarly replace VM tags.
  Tags may be omitted at all levels. An explicit empty disk tags map disables inheritance.
- A supplied `private_ip_address` forces static allocation. Otherwise allocation defaults to `Dynamic`.
  No public IP address, network security group, or remote-access service is created.
- Data-disk keys must be stable at plan time. LUNs must be unique within each VM and between 0 and 63.
  Set a data disk's zone explicitly when required; it does not inherit the VM's zone.
- Backup include/exclude LUN sets are mutually exclusive and can reference only LUNs declared in that VM's `data_disks`.
  Creating a protection association is not evidence that a backup or restore has completed.
- VM outputs are maps keyed by the VM input keys. Disk outputs are nested maps keyed by VM and disk keys.
  Backup outputs contain only VMs with backup configured; disk maps are empty for VMs without additional disks.

## Telemetry

Telemetry is enabled by default. Set `enable_telemetry = false` on the module call to disable it in both the root and child module.
With telemetry enabled, `location` is used for telemetry, falling back to the first VM's resolved location when omitted.
An empty VM map therefore still requires `location` unless telemetry is disabled.

Both modules create an empty Azure deployment at the active subscription scope for telemetry.
The deployment identity needs `Microsoft.Resources/deployments/read`, `write`, and `delete` permissions at that scope.
Telemetry deployment failures fail the apply. These deployments intentionally update on normal applies,
even when the VM configuration is unchanged. See [AVM telemetry guidance](https://aka.ms/avm/telemetryinfo).

## Development

See the [tests guide](tests/README.md) for validation commands and coverage, and the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md)
for contribution policies. Use PowerShell 7.4 or later with [Avm.Authoring](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools#install).
Edit `_header.md`, `_footer.md`, and variable/output descriptions, then run `avm docs` to regenerate the module and example README files.
The directory indexes in `examples/README.md`, `modules/README.md`, and `tests/README.md` are authored guides.
Run `avm pre-commit`, review its changes, and run `avm pr-check` only after committing your intended changes and obtaining a clean worktree.

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_confidential_virtual_machines"></a> [confidential\_virtual\_machines](#input\_confidential\_virtual\_machines)

Description: Map of confidential virtual machine definitions for the pattern.

Keys identify VM instances and must be known at plan time. Values are objects:

- `name` - (Required) Name of the virtual machine.
- `resource_group_name` - (Required) Existing resource group name for the VM, NIC, and data disks.
- `subnet_resource_id` - (Required) Subnet resource ID used by the primary NIC IP configuration.
- `source_image_reference` - (Required) Source image reference for the virtual machine.
  - `publisher` - (Required) Image publisher.
  - `offer` - (Required) Image offer.
  - `sku` - (Required) Confidential-compute-compatible image SKU.
  - `version` - (Required) Image version or `latest`.
- `location` - (Optional) Region for the VM and NIC. If omitted, module-level `location` is used.
- `os_type` - (Optional) VM operating system type: `Linux` or `Windows`. Defaults to `Linux`.
- `zone` - (Optional) Availability zone for the virtual machine.
- `size` - (Optional) VM size. Defaults to `Standard_DC2as_v5`.
- `admin_username` - (Optional) Admin username. Defaults to `azureuser`.
- `admin_password` - (Optional) Admin password. Required for Windows. Optional for Linux when SSH key is provided.
- `admin_ssh_public_key` - (Optional) SSH public key for Linux.
- `secure_boot_enabled` - (Optional) Enable secure boot. Defaults to `true`.
- `vtpm_enabled` - (Optional) Enable vTPM. Defaults to `true`.
- `private_ip_address` - (Optional) Private IP for the primary NIC IP configuration. Supplying a value forces static allocation.
- `private_ip_address_allocation` - (Optional) `Dynamic` or `Static`. Defaults to `Dynamic`.
- `network_interface_name` - (Optional) NIC name. Defaults to `<name>-nic`.
- `accelerated_networking_enabled` - (Optional) Whether accelerated networking is enabled on the NIC. Defaults to `false`.
- `computer_name` - (Optional) OS hostname; when omitted, the provider uses the VM name subject to OS naming constraints.
- `identity_type` - (Optional) Managed identity type: `SystemAssigned`, `UserAssigned`, or `SystemAssigned, UserAssigned`. Defaults to `SystemAssigned`.
- `user_assigned_identity_resource_ids` - (Optional) User-assigned identity IDs, only used when `identity_type` includes `UserAssigned`.
- `tags` - (Optional) Tags applied to VM and NIC resources. If omitted, module-level `tags` is used. Maps replace rather than merge.
- `backup_configuration` - (Optional) Azure Backup configuration:
  - `recovery_vault_resource_group_name` - (Required) Resource group name of the Recovery Services vault.
  - `recovery_vault_name` - (Required) Name of the Recovery Services vault.
  - `backup_policy_resource_id` - (Required) Compatible backup policy resource ID to associate with the VM. Use an Enhanced (`V2`) policy when required by the VM configuration. For daily/weekly Enhanced policies, explicitly configure instant-restore retention shorter than vaulted retention. The module does not create or convert policies.
  - `include_disk_luns` - (Optional) Declared data-disk LUNs to include in backup. Mutually exclusive with `exclude_disk_luns`.
  - `exclude_disk_luns` - (Optional) Declared data-disk LUNs to exclude from backup. Mutually exclusive with `include_disk_luns`.
- `data_disks` - (Optional) Map of additional managed data disks (zero to many) created and attached to the VM:
  - `name` - (Optional) Managed disk name. Defaults to `<vm-name>-<disk-key>`.
  - `lun` - (Required) Data disk LUN between 0 and 63, unique within this VM.
  - `disk_size_gb` - (Required) Data disk size in GB.
  - `storage_account_type` - (Optional) Storage SKU. Defaults to `Premium_LRS`.
  - `caching` - (Optional) Host caching mode (`None`, `ReadOnly`, `ReadWrite`). Defaults to `ReadWrite`.
  - `zone` - (Optional) Availability zone for the managed disk. Does not inherit the VM zone.
  - `disk_encryption_set_id` - (Optional) Disk encryption set resource ID.
  - `write_accelerator_enabled` - (Optional) Enables write accelerator on the attachment. Defaults to `false`.
  - `tags` - (Optional) Tags for the data disk resource, replacing VM tags when supplied. Inherits VM tags when omitted; may be omitted at all levels.
- `os_disk` - (Optional) Confidential OS disk options:
  - `caching` - (Optional) OS disk caching type. Defaults to `ReadWrite`.
  - `storage_account_type` - (Optional) OS disk storage account type. Defaults to `Premium_LRS`.
  - `disk_size_gb` - (Optional) OS disk size in GB.
  - `security_encryption_type` - (Optional) Confidential OS disk encryption type: `VMGuestStateOnly` or `DiskWithVMGuestState`. Defaults to `DiskWithVMGuestState`.
  - `secure_vm_disk_encryption_set_id` - (Optional) Disk encryption set resource ID for confidential disk encryption with customer-managed keys.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                = string
    resource_group_name = string
    subnet_resource_id  = string
    source_image_reference = object({
      publisher = string
      offer     = string
      sku       = string
      version   = string
    })

    location                            = optional(string, null)
    os_type                             = optional(string, "Linux")
    zone                                = optional(string, null)
    size                                = optional(string, "Standard_DC2as_v5")
    admin_username                      = optional(string, "azureuser")

    admin_ssh_public_key                = optional(string, null)
    secure_boot_enabled                 = optional(bool, true)
    vtpm_enabled                        = optional(bool, true)
    private_ip_address                  = optional(string, null)
    private_ip_address_allocation       = optional(string, "Dynamic")
    network_interface_name              = optional(string, null)
    accelerated_networking_enabled      = optional(bool, false)
    computer_name                       = optional(string, null)
    identity_type                       = optional(string, "SystemAssigned")
    user_assigned_identity_resource_ids = optional(set(string), [])
    tags                                = optional(map(string), null)
    backup_configuration = optional(object({
      recovery_vault_resource_group_name = string

      backup_policy_resource_id          = string
      include_disk_luns                  = optional(set(number), null)
      exclude_disk_luns                  = optional(set(number), null)
    }), null)
    data_disks = optional(map(object({
      name                      = optional(string, null)
      lun                       = number
      disk_size_gb              = number
      storage_account_type      = optional(string, "Premium_LRS")

  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_enable_telemetry"></a> [enable\_telemetry](#input\_enable\_telemetry)

Description: This variable controls whether or not telemetry is enabled for the module.  
For more information see <https://aka.ms/avm/telemetryinfo>.  
If it is set to false, then no telemetry will be collected.

Type: `bool`

Default: `true`

### <a name="input_location"></a> [location](#input\_location)

Description: Default Azure region for VMs that omit location and for telemetry. When omitted, every VM needs its own location and telemetry uses the first VM's resolved location. Required for an empty VM map when telemetry is enabled.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_tags"></a> [tags](#input\_tags)

Description: Default tags for VMs and NICs when VM-level tags are omitted. VM tags replace this map rather than merge with it. Data disks inherit VM tags unless disk-level tags are supplied. Tags may be omitted at all levels.

Type: `map(string)`

Default: `null`

## Outputs

The following outputs are exported:

### <a name="output_backup_protected_vm_ids"></a> [backup\_protected\_vm\_ids](#output\_backup\_protected\_vm\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of Azure Backup protected-item associations for confidential virtual machines.

### <a name="output_confidential_virtual_machine_private_ip_addresses"></a> [confidential\_virtual\_machine\_private\_ip\_addresses](#output\_confidential\_virtual\_machine\_private\_ip\_addresses)

Description: Primary private IP addresses for confidential virtual machines.

### <a name="output_confidential_virtual_machine_resource_ids"></a> [confidential\_virtual\_machine\_resource\_ids](#output\_confidential\_virtual\_machine\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of confidential virtual machines.

### <a name="output_confidential_virtual_machine_resource_names"></a> [confidential\_virtual\_machine\_resource\_names](#output\_confidential\_virtual\_machine\_resource\_names)

Description: Resource names of confidential virtual machines.

### <a name="output_data_disk_attachment_resource_ids"></a> [data\_disk\_attachment\_resource\_ids](#output\_data\_disk\_attachment\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of data disk attachments for confidential virtual machines, grouped by VM key and data-disk key.

### <a name="output_data_disk_resource_ids"></a> [data\_disk\_resource\_ids](#output\_data\_disk\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of managed data disks for confidential virtual machines, grouped by VM key and data-disk key.

### <a name="output_network_interface_resource_ids"></a> [network\_interface\_resource\_ids](#output\_network\_interface\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of network interfaces created for confidential virtual machines.

### <a name="output_system_assigned_identity_principal_ids"></a> [system\_assigned\_identity\_principal\_ids](#output\_system\_assigned\_identity\_principal\_ids)

Description: System-assigned managed identity principal IDs keyed by VM key. Only meaningful for VMs with a system-assigned identity.
